recipes.title: Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Crisp buttermilk fried chicken with a seasoned flour coating.
recipes.notes: Keep the oil at 350°F and do not crowd the pan, or the coating will go soggy.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk for at least 30 minutes.
Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Lift the chicken from the buttermilk, letting the excess drip off, and dredge it in the seasoned flour.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry the chicken in batches for 12-15 minutes, until golden and 165°F inside.
Drain on a rack and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Lasagna
recipes.description: Layered pasta with a beef-tomato sauce, ricotta, and melted mozzarella.
recipes.notes: Resting for 10 minutes before slicing keeps the layers from sliding apart.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and cook the noodles until just tender, then drain.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic, drain, then stir in the tomato sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, egg, parmesan, and Italian seasoning.
In a baking dish, layer sauce, noodles, ricotta mixture, and mozzarella, repeating and finishing with sauce and mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for 15 more minutes until bubbly. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Butter Tarts
recipes.description: Canadian butter tarts with flaky pastry and a gooey brown sugar and maple filling.
recipes.notes: The centres should still be slightly wobbly when they come out of the oven; they set as they cool.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and place the tart shells in a muffin tin.
Whisk the butter, brown sugar, maple syrup, eggs, vinegar, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Drop a few raisins into each shell, then fill each shell about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18-20 minutes, until the filling is set at the edges and still slightly wobbly in the centre.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.
